\mxnewpage\section*{Solutions EV2-B}\label{EV2-B-CORR}
\textbf{MCQ:} 1 A, 2 C, 3 D, 4 B, 5 A, 6 B, 7 C, 8 C, 9 A, 10 D, 11 D, 12 C. Each correct answer: 0.5 point; total 6.
\paragraph{Checks of the fluency questions.} Order of operations; sum of fractions; subtraction of exponents; multiplying coefficient 1.2; division by 0.8; product 1.25 times 0.8; solving an affine equation; vertical increment divided by horizontal; mean; angle divided by 360; complement to 1; substitution in brackets.
\subsection*{Exercise 1 -- Independence and repetition}
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dfrac{1}{6}$ and $\dfrac{1}{4}+\dfrac{2}{3}-\dfrac{1}{6}=\dfrac{3}{4}$. \textit{Marking: 1 point. Result and basic justification expected; half a point possible for a correct but unfinished approach.}
\item Three paths, each $(\dfrac{1}{4})^2(\dfrac{3}{4})$: total $\dfrac{9}{64}$. \textit{Marking: 2 points. Method or justification: 1; calculation and conclusion: 1.}
\item Complement of three failures: $1-(\dfrac{3}{4})^3=\dfrac{37}{64}$. \textit{Marking: 2 points. Method or justification: 1; calculation and conclusion: 1.}
\end{enumerate}
\subsection*{Exercise 2 -- Rational function and symmetry}
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f=x+\dfrac{4}{x}$, odd. \textit{Marking: 1 point. Result and basic justification expected; half a point possible for a correct but unfinished approach.}
\item $f\prime =\dfrac{x^2-4}{x^2}$; decreasing up to 2 then increasing. \textit{Marking: 2 points. Method or justification: 1; calculation and conclusion: 1.}
\item Increasing on $]-\infty;-2]$, decreasing on $[-2;0[$. On $[1;2]$, f decreases: a counterexample to global increase. \textit{Marking: 2 points. Method or justification: 1; calculation and conclusion: 1.}
\end{enumerate}
\subsection*{Exercise 3 -- Distance and parameter}

\item Distance $\dfrac{12}{5}$; $x^2+y^2=\dfrac{144}{25}$. \textit{Marking: 2 points. Method or justification: 1; calculation and conclusion: 1.}
